newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Jan 14.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Jan 14.

text.p: Two of Mexico's crude shipping ports remained closed for a second day due to high winds, and six Gulf of Mexico ports in total were shut, the Communications and Transport Ministry said in its daily report 1000 local/1600 GMT Tuesday.
Pajaritos, under the jurisdiction of Coatzacoalcos in Veracruz state, was still closed amid winds between 40 to 55 km per hour. The port shut Monday at 0440 local/1040 GMT.
Dos Bocas in Tabasco state remained closed after shutting 0600 local/1200 GMT Monday, with winds of 50 to 60 km per hour.
The largest of Mexico's crude ports, Cayo Arcas in Campeche state, remained open although winds were reported in the region at between 35 and 45 km per hour.

Pajaritos ships an average 400,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude and Dos Bocas exports 300,000 bpd, according to the latest oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) statistics. Cayo Arcas ships an average 600,000 bpd.
Tamaulipas port Tuxpan, Tabasco port Frontera, and Campeche port were reported shut amid winds of up to 75 km per hour.
Tampico, Veracruz, Progreso and Salina Cruz ports were closed to smaller boats amid winds between 20 and 40 km per hour.
The report also warned against sailing in the Gulf of Mexico and the Gulf of Tehuantepec because of winds and high waves.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.

Light rains along the coasts of Baja California, Sonora, Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima, Michoacan and Guerrero. Winds from the north at 10 to 20 knots (19 to 38 kilometers/11 to 22 miles per hour) and waves four to six feet high.
Winds in the Gulf of Tehuantepec at 15 to 25 knots (28 to 47 km/17 to 28 miles per hour) with waves seven to nine feet high.

A stationary cold front moving south toward the Yucatan peninsula with a mass of cold air and disperse rains. Winds from the northeast at 20 to 25 knots (38 to 47 km/22 to 28 miles per hour) and waves nine to 11 feet high.

Semi-stationary cold front with clouds and light rains along the coast of Quintana Roo and Central America. Winds from the east and northeast at 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 17 miles per hour) and waves three to five feet high.
